main_body: Round stone tower: a green scalloped conical roof (rows 2-39) over a grey brick wall (rows 42-93) with a window and an arched wooden door
top_band: Green shingled conical roof slope, rows ~2-39, light green at the upper left shading to dark teal at the right. It ends at a brown eave band with a dark underside at rows 40-41.
evidence: Down the middle column there is a large roof slope with shingle rows, then a brown eave lip and a dark shadow row at 40-41, then the grey brick wall. The roof reads as a visible sloped top surface in the same way as the reference house roofs. The window has a frame, a sill with plants and dark inner glazing. The door has a stone surround and a dark lintel edge. The wall itself is flat front-facing, but the overhanging roof and eave shadow carry the 3/4 reading.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 green steps with per-shingle highlights and dark-green outlines, comparable to the reference tile roofs. The stone wall has 3-4 tones, with bricks separated by dark purple-grey mortar lines and a darker right side. Outlines are tinted to the neighbouring material (dark green, dark grey-violet, dark brown), not black. The bricks are individually shaded but their faces are quite smooth, with less speckle than the reference plaster and cobble. The door and window have decent detail. Overall it is slightly less dense than the references but would sit acceptably beside them.
